name: Burning Coal Vein / Elkhorn Corridor Dispersed Camping - Little Missouri Grassland

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Medora Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general grassland dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted on general Little Missouri National Grassland public lands. Must park within 30ft of public forest roads. Driving off-road prohibited.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in prairie/badland soil, 200 feet from dry washes. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood; badland prairie wood gathering non-existent.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in containerized fire pans or existing rock rings only due to extreme prairie fire hazard. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Red Flag Warning fire bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel and dirt prairie road (East River Road / FS 739)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel road crossing clay badlands. Can turn slick gumbo clay when wet.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible along main gravel roads in dry weather; high clearance recommended for side spurs)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low to Moderate (Badland scoria ridges create mild line of sight shadows)

services_available: Theodore Roosevelt National Park Visitor Center

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 50-65°F, high winds, spring rain turning badland clay to gumbo mud.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (85-95°F), intense solar heat, late afternoon prairie thunderstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal badlands boondocking season (55-70°F daytime, 30-40°F nights), crisp clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe sub-zero Northern Plains winter (-10 to 20°F), heavy blowing snow.

dangers_and_hazards: Prairie wildfires during dry Red Flag Warnings
Clay badland roads becoming impassable gumbo mud when wet
Prairie Rattlesnakes active in warm months

common_human_made_sounds: Infrequent ranch truck on gravel road
Wind blowing through scoria badland ridges

common_animals: Bison / American Buffalo (Bison bison in nearby Theodore Roosevelt NP)

human_demographics_and_culture: Maah Daah Hey Trail mountain bikers, Theodore Roosevelt history buffs, solar digital nomads, and badlands astrophotographers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara (Three Affiliated Tribes) indigenous traditions honor the Little Missouri Badlands as sacred spirit grounds and ancestral fasting sites.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Red scoria rock badland energy, profound spatial silence, pristine Bortle 1 night skies.
